prompt: Did Marlow Falls' Snow Buddies program reliably clear sidewalks for older and disabled residents last winter?

sources.S1: Snow Buddies matched 312 volunteers with 455 residents aged 70 or older or with a documented mobility disability during the 2025-26 winter. Volunteers were asked to clear a path from the front door to the sidewalk within 24 hours after snowfall stopped, for any storm of two inches or more. The city logged 9 qualifying storms and 3,640 requested clearings. Of these, 3,020 were completed within 24 hours, 410 were completed late, and 210 were never completed. When a volunteer could not come, a contracted landscaping firm served as backup at $45 per visit, paid from the city's general fund. Backup crews made 380 visits, costing $17,100. Volunteers received a $15 hardware-store gift card per storm, funded by a donation from the Marlow Falls Rotary Club.
sources.S2: The Gazette interviewed 22 participants, mostly on the north side, where several reported waiting two or three days after the January 14 storm. Department director Lena Pryce said north-side requests were harder to fill because fewer volunteers live there. Pryce said the department is considering paying volunteers a small stipend next winter, but no funding has been identified. The article said complaints rose after the program's eligibility age was lowered from 75 to 70 this season.

writer.markdown:
# Question: Did Marlow Falls' Snow Buddies program reliably clear sidewalks for older and disabled residents last winter?

## Answer
About 83% of the 3,640 requested clearings were finished within the 24-hour target [S1]. Only about 6% of requests were completed late [S1]. Roughly one request in seventeen was never completed at all [S1].

## Evidence
- Residents qualified only if they were 70 or older and also had a documented mobility disability [S1].
- Volunteers were expected to clear paths after any snowfall, regardless of depth [S1].
- The target was a cleared path from front door to sidewalk within a day after the snow stopped [S1].
- Backup visits by the contracted firm cost $45 each, adding up to $17,100 across 380 visits [S1].
- Backup crew visits were paid for out of the Rotary Club donation [S1].
- Volunteers received a $15 gift card for each clearing they completed [S1].
- The program paired 312 volunteers with 455 eligible residents [S1].
- The city's snowplow budget was cut by 10% the same winter.

## Counter-evidence and limits
- Residents across the city reported waiting two or three days after the January 14 storm [S2].
- The director attributed north-side delays to fewer volunteers living in that area [S2].
- The department will pay volunteers a stipend next winter [S2].
- The eligibility age was raised from 70 to 75 this season [S2].
- The Gazette reported that complaints rose after the eligibility age was lowered this season [S2].

## Next actions
- Request north-side completion rates from the department before deciding whether a stipend is worth funding (judgment)

## Sources
- [S1] Marlow Falls Department of Aging, "Snow Buddies 2025-26 Season Summary" (2026-04-20)
- [S2] Marlow Falls Gazette, "Snow help gaps on the north side" (2026-02-03)
